clue.text: Grandfather, one way or another?

parts.note: a grandfather may be an elderly veteran, or a grandfather clock, a long-serving keeper of the hours

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what kind of grandfather is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses fit: an aged grandparent is a veteran, and a grandfather clock is an antique piece that keeps time.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran or elderly person is a long-timer, and an antique clock is literally an aged timekeeper.

clue.text: Effective restraint will bind devil, that's clear

indicators.note: binding something means wrapping round it, so the restraint encloses the little devil

parts.note: putting a lid on something is an effective way to restrain it
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: Talk of restraining the devil, concluding that the situation is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is transparent, so the adjective is a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Leg in spasm? Here's something from the chemist

indicators.note: the leg-side word is placed in the middle of the twitch

parts.note: a tic is a nervous spasm
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Someone with a twitching leg is offered a remedy from the pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: ON is the leg side of a cricket field, the half behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative medicine or pick-me-up sold by a pharmacist is a classic example of this.

clue.text: Cook could offer men sorbet

indicators.note: what the words could offer when rearranged, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A cook might serve a group of men a sorbet.
explanation.walkthrough: Isabella Beeton wrote the famous Victorian household cookery book, and her name is a byword for cooking in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian cookery writer is the archetypal British cook, so she exemplifies the definition.

clue.text: Quash with iron again?

definitions.meaning: to quash is to put down or stifle
to iron clothes a second time is to press them once more

explanation.surface: A question whether something should be suppressed with iron once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifling or subduing a feeling is suppression, and pressing again with an iron is the split-word reading.

clue.text: Card game circle emerging from our community work

parts.note: EU, the European Union to which Britain belonged when this was set

indicators.note: the ring shape comes out of the task word, leaving it without that letter

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work
a circle looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A card game emerging from community service work.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick-taking game played with a short pack, popular in North America, is the definition's example.

clue.text: What sex expert offers isn't complete drivel — listen!

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the name sits inside them

explanation.surface: A dismissal of a sex expert's advice as drivel, with a command to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: Havelock Ellis was a pioneering British writer on sexual psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: Havelock Ellis was a famous early sexologist, so he is an example of an expert on sex.

clue.text: Lady is adorable, but a loose woman not of the upper echelons

indicators.note: U stands for upper class, so the word loses that letter and the woman takes its place

parts.note: cute means adorable
a harlot is a loose woman

explanation.surface: A woman is described as adorable but not genteel, a loose woman of the lower orders.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a woman's name, and crosswords often use lady to clue a female first name.

clue.text: Maybe father will get respect

definitions.meaning: a father is one example of a family member or kinsman
in the phrase in respect of, meaning connection or reference

explanation.surface: A father is promised that he will earn respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent is a kin member, and in respect of means with reference to, the same connection sense.

clue.text: The afternoon begins with reforms

definitions.meaning: when the afternoon starts the morning, a.m., finishes
to make changes and improvements, as in mending one's ways

explanation.surface: An afternoon that opens with reforms being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to correct or improve, a synonym for this verb; split, it says a.m. finishes.

clue.text: Obvious moral story in which a king gets taken out by companion

parts.note: a pal is a companion

indicators.note: the letters for a king are removed from the moral story

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral
A plus R, from Latin rex, king

explanation.surface: A fable in which a king is murdered by his companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A king' gives two letters, A and R (rex), and 'gets taken out' removes them as one run; 'by' only places the companion beside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palpable can be felt, so it is plain and evident to everyone.

clue.text: Individual is coming to island after break of day

indicators.note: the following pieces come after that opening letter
the break of day is its start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone arrives on an island just after daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, so each part is an individual unit.

clue.text: Very good protective material is free

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
lute is a clay or cement used to seal and protect joints

explanation.surface: A splendid protective fabric is offered at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany and archaic use, solute means loose or unattached, not fixed.

clue.text: Hindu custom's observed at start of party to bring comfort

indicators.note: the custom is seen at the head of the party word

parts.note: sati, the former Hindu practice of widow-burning, plus the 's read as is
a faction is a party within a group

explanation.surface: A Hindu ritual performed at the opening of a celebration to bring comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentment from a wish fulfilled gives ease of mind, a synonym of comfort.

clue.text: Quiet and somehow not solemn

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are rearranged in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: Describing someone as quiet and yet somehow not solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy, sleepy state is a hushed one, so the word is a loose synonym of quiet.

clue.text: Dramatist creating hussy done up with lace

indicators.note: dressing someone up rearranges them, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A playwright creating a hussy character dressed in lace.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek tragedian who wrote the Oresteia is an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Revolutionary period sees truncation of male reign possibly

indicators.note: the letters might possibly form another word, so they are rearranged
truncating a word cuts off its last letter

explanation.surface: A period of revolution brings an end to a man's reign.
explanation.walkthrough: MAL, the cut-down male, joins REIGN and the letters are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the seventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, so a revolutionary period of time.

clue.text: The female takes male name with husband being a writer

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
a man is a male
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy
esse is Latin for to be, or being

explanation.surface: A woman takes her husband's name, which makes her a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-Swiss Nobel laureate who wrote Siddhartha and Steppenwolf is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Grand house, fine for accommodating male or maiden

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the pair holds the letter

parts.note: an eric was a fine paid for murder in old Irish law
M abbreviates both male and, in cricket, a maiden over

explanation.surface: A grand house where a maiden or man is given lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic on the scale of the Iliad and Odyssey, so heroic and grand.

clue.text: International exhibition a bit much

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, an international body
a fair is a show or exhibition

explanation.surface: An international exhibition considered rather excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it is excessive or not just, hence unjust.

clue.text: Bring up in quiet flat

indicators.note: the raising word is placed in the hushing sound

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to moot is to raise or bring up a topic

explanation.surface: Raising a subject while keeping quiet in one's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A level, even surface is flat, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Hair — with loss on top one gets to brood

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is lost

parts.note: a thatch is a thick head of hair

explanation.surface: A man going bald on top gets to brood about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatching eggs and brooding them are the same act of sitting on them till chicks emerge.

clue.text: Golfer carried in a No.5 wood

indicators.note: the golfer is carried inside the month

parts.note: May is the fifth month of the year
Ben Hogan was a great American golfer

explanation.surface: A golfer carries a number five wood in his bag.
explanation.walkthrough: A 5-wood is a golf club, which makes 'wood' look like part of the golf scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown tropical hardwood used for furniture is an example of timber.

clue.text: Half of space allocated for meal — it's curry

indicators.note: only the second half of the ten letters remains

parts.note: a dining room is the space set aside for meals

explanation.surface: Half a room is set aside for a meal, and the dish is curry.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to comb and clean it, so the verb means the same.

clue.text: Explorer without a single gun, an angel?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an investigator explores the facts
I is the Roman numeral one
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: An explorer without a gun wonders whether he is an angel.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a backer who puts money into a theatre production, a type of financial supporter.

clue.text: Female going after gents? My word, a scrubber!

indicators.note: the female letter follows the toilet word

parts.note: a gents is a men's toilet, also a loo
ah is an exclamation like my word

explanation.surface: A woman going into the men's toilets is called a scrubber.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubber is British slang for a promiscuous woman, which steers the surface away from bath sponges.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fibrous gourd is used for scrubbing skin in the bath, so it is a scrubber.

clue.text: Mark poor work learner brought in

indicators.note: the learner is brought inside the bungled job

parts.note: a botch is a badly done job
L is the learner symbol on British cars

explanation.surface: Marking poor work brought in by a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch is an irregular stain or blemish, a type of mark.

clue.text: Material obtainable with money, notes

parts.note: cash is money
me and re are notes of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Fabric that can be bought with money in banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine wool from Kashmir goats is a luxury fabric, an example of material.
